Red dot = apex; red dashed line = blast crossing (KO). Spike moves (negative angle) launch from 3 m up (off-stage scenario) so the downward send is visible.

DI escape-space

The baseline launch plus the same launch with the victim holding one DI direction through hitstun — baseline in (MoveY −1, toward attacker) away (MoveY +1) up (MoveX +1) down (MoveX −1) — rotated by the sim's real ApplyDirectionalInfluence (18° cap, Melee sin² curve; perpendicular holds bend most; in/away on horizontal sends only push via ASDI). Escape magnitude = max launch-vector deviation in the caption: low = DI-resistant (reliable combo/kill tool), high = DI-bendable (escapable). Common scale across the character; pick the victim % above each figure's grid.

KO & blast clearance

kill % = lowest victim % at which the launch crosses a blast line before landing (— = no KO by 250%). Clearance = fraction of the way to the top / side blast line at the highest simulated %, so a move that can't kill still shows how close it gets.

Authored hitbox reach

Side-view overlay of the authored hitbox volumes across the active frames, resolved with the real HitboxGeometry.ResolvePositions at the grounded origin frame (yaw 0 → forward = +Z). Character silhouette = capsule (2× radius wide). Colored capsule lines per hit, one per active tick (opacity 0.18 — overlap darkens, so the union reads). Bands = thirds of capsule height from the feet (high +0.5 m headroom); reach = max forward (Z) extent over the bands. Gaps = per-height whiff zones below the kit's max reach at that height; uncovered bands = no normal reaches them.

True-combo reachability

Pure reachability (no scripted routes, no recommendations): for each normal × hit state × %, the starter connects through the real hit path, then the attacker plays a greedy chase and presses each follow-up as soon as actionable + in reach. Cell: T = follow-up landed while the victim was still in hitstun (true combo) · F = landed after stun expired (opponent actionable) · – = never connected. tight = window tightness per % — sim stun (0.5 × launch speed) − (recovery + landing lag + jump squat + follow-up trigger); positive = frame-true on paper (travel + hitstop make reality ≤ paper). The sim derives hitstun from launch speed; the authored StunTicks is a zero/nonzero gate only, so tightness grows as the victim takes damage. Hover a cell for connect tick / stun left / tightness.
Combo density — total true links (all starters × follow-ups × hit states) per victim %: a tuning target for too-combo-heavy vs too-sparse. No threshold is hardcoded; the number is yours to read.
